goal:
Add orbit prediction to the Universe Sandbox game in Sandbox/UniverseSandbox.

When a body is selected, draw the path it is predicted to follow: integrate a throwaway copy of the simulation forward a few hundred steps without disturbing the live one, and draw the resulting points as a fading trail ahead of the body. The prediction must account for gravity from all other bodies, and must stop early if the body would be absorbed by a black hole or merge with something.

Wire it in end to end:
- physics.py: a pure predict_path(bodies, index, steps) helper that returns the predicted points and never mutates the live simulation state.
- render/: draw the predicted path for the selected body, fading with distance along the path.
- ui.py: a 'Predict' toggle in the toolbar, next to the existing toggles.
- main.py: wire the toggle so the path appears and disappears.
- _smoke_test.py: add checks that predict_path leaves the live bodies untouched, that a circular orbit predicts a path returning near its start, and that a body aimed into a black hole predicts a truncated path.

Work module by module and re-run the smoke test as you go, rather than surveying everything before making any change. Use palette.py for any colours you need rather than adding new literals.

Verify by running: python _smoke_test.py in Sandbox/UniverseSandbox. Every existing check must still pass unchanged - do not weaken, remove or rewrite any of them - and your new prediction checks must pass too. Delete any temporary scripts you create.
